verdict.reasoning: Patient reports left arm numbness and tingling and difficulty with fine motor tasks: “I can't quite move my left arm… it's numb, and then I also feel some, like tingling in my fingertips” and notes difficulty hitting piano notes, indicating decreased dexterity.
Patient states: “It's probably been, I'd say, for at least two weeks, and it's kind of gotten worse,” indicating onset about 2 weeks ago and progressive symptoms.

Patient describes distribution: “I can feel it both in my… a little bit in my elbow, and then in my arm, as well as in my hand” and specifies “it's my second, third, and fourth finger… it's the… front side,” i.e., palmar digits 2–4 from elbow to hand.

Patient reports subjective weakness with function: “I will say… I play a little bit of a piano and so I just noticed it's been kind of harder to get the notes,” and confirms it is weakness due to numbness, not pain.

Regarding shoulder symptoms: “sometimes I will feel it in my shoulder. Like if I try to… move like in boxing and stuff, I will even… maybe feel a little bit of… pain,” indicating intermittent shoulder discomfort with boxing movements.
Patient states: “I tried to get a massage, it's not better. Or… warm baths. It's not better,” showing no relief from massage or warm baths.

Neck pain: Patient first says “Yes, absolutely. No, not, no, nothing,” effectively denying neck pain; she also denies seizures and loss of consciousness: “Ohh, no, no, no, no, nothing like that,” and weakness is limited to the left arm: “your weakness is only in your left arm. Legs are… normal, yeah? … Yeah, yeah, yeah, walking is normal,” supporting denial of leg weakness, seizures, and LOC.

Patient describes: “I all of a sudden just couldn't see from… my left eye… I lost some… field of vision… that just lasted maybe for… twenty minutes?” and later confirms “maybe like twenty minutes or so… when I woke up it was gone,” indicating transient left peripheral vision loss lasting ~20 minutes, now resolved, occurring “a few weeks ago.”

Patient history: “I also had a really bad cold, like a month ago… I was sick for probably good like two weeks. I think I must have had some kind of like a flu or something.” She also notes “sometimes I get headaches but I think they're just tired headaches… I just kind of feel this fatigue… this morning… I just felt really, fatigued and I couldn't even get myself to the gym,” supporting a prior 2‑week cold/flu, current fatigue, and occasional tired headaches.
Regarding overall health: “in general, I'm, I'm pretty healthy… I don't really have any medical problems,” indicating denial of chronic conditions.
Medication use: “I do take Ibuprofen because my muscles were sore… So… my knuckles on my right hand… I've just kind of taken ibuprofen for that,” indicating ibuprofen as needed.
Patient says: “Not really. I just take ibuprofen every once in a while, I take vitamin D,” confirming vitamin D use.
Patient notes: “my GP really wants me to take iron supplements, but… they're just like huge pills so I… most of the time I just forget,” indicating iron with poor adherence.
Patient adds: “And then, sometimes I take Melatonin to help me sleep,” consistent with melatonin as needed.

Family history: “I know that my dad has I don't know if it it's hypo, I think it's hypothyroidism… he's got some autoimmune stuff going on,” supporting hypothyroidism and an autoimmune condition in father.
For mother: “my mom… she's got diabetes type two. She's got hypertension… she's got high cholesterol,” which corresponds to type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia.
Activity: “I've started taking this boxing class. I've been taking this boxing class for a few weeks,” and later “I work out,” indicating boxing classes and regular exercise.
Alcohol episode: “we were like out partying until… late hours, and I just got uncharacteristically drunk for me,” indicating a recent single heavy drinking episode.

Transcript: left arm paresthesia and weakness for at least 2 weeks and worsening (“It's probably been… at least two weeks, and it's kind of gotten worse”), and doctor explicitly suspects neurologic etiology beyond boxing: “I'm just wondering whether there's something a bit more than just the boxing here… that with the weakness of the arms, make me think, is there something else going on rather than just an injury?”

Doctor links transient visual loss to neuro workup and urgency: “you do get things like MS… can have, visual problems, like what you've experienced… I'm going to do an urgent, very urgent neurology referral… what that might entail is the brain scan and things like that,” which reflects that the transient left visual field loss is treated as a neuro‑ophthalmic event needing urgent evaluation.

Patient gives temporal sequence: heavy drinking → “then after that, I was sick for probably good like two weeks… some kind of like a flu,” and later mentions fatigue and neurological symptoms in the same time frame. The doctor acknowledges concern that “there's something a bit more than just the boxing here,” supporting that a recent viral illness and fatigue are temporally associated with current neurologic concerns.

Right hand symptoms: “I kind of hurt like my knuckles on my right hand. So that's been a little bit painful, so I've just kind of taken ibuprofen for that,” indicating minor right knuckle pain from boxing managed with ibuprofen.
Doctor states: “I'm going to do an urgent, very urgent neurology referral,” matching an advised urgent neurology referral.
Doctor explains: “What they… might entail is the brain scan and things like that,” indicating likely brain imaging as part of the neurological workup.

Treatment discussion: “The treatment for it is actually some steroids… when you have an acute… reaction… But… first we need to firm diagnosis,” and “that's something we can't do,” indicating no steroids or disease‑specific therapy until diagnosis is confirmed.

ED/A&E advice: “if there's any weakness… progresses to your legs, or there's any kind of headaches, vomiting, fits, and your visual symptoms are getting worse and not getting better, then that would be an A and E,” which aligns with worsening weakness, severe headache, vomiting, seizures (fits), or worsening/recurring visual symptoms as ED precautions.

The plan in the transcript does not explicitly state to continue current symptomatic measures (e.g., massage, warm baths, ibuprofen); these are only described as having been tried and not helpful. No advice is given to continue them, so recommending continuation is an added plan detail.
